title: Collapsibility of Performance Metrics in Clinical Predictive AI
abstract: arXiv:2608.30568v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Background: Population level assessments of predictive artificial intelligence (AI) can conceal performance disparities across subgroups. Fairness evaluations commonly rely on performance analyses across subgroups. However, some performance metrics are non-collapsible, meaning that the overall population performance value does not equal the weighted average of subgroup specific values.   Objective: To examine the collapsibility properties of commonly reported performance metrics in predictive AI, with a focus on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, also known as c-statistic).   Methods: We investigate the collapsibility of 15 performance metrics, either by expressing each metric as a linear combination of its stratum specific values or, where non-collapsible, by providing a counterexample inspired by Simpson's paradox as a formal disproof. translated_title: 临床预测AI中性能指标的可合并性
translated_abstract: 背景：对预测人工智能（AI）的群体层面评估可能掩盖各亚组之间的性能差异。公平性评估通常依赖于跨亚组的性能分析。然而，一些性能指标是不可合并的（non-collapsible），这意味着总体人群的性能值不等于各亚组特定值的加权平均。目的：考察预测AI中常报告的性能指标的可合并性属性，重点关注受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUC，也称为c统计量）。方法：我们研究了15个性能指标的可合并性，方法是将每个指标表示为其各层特定值的线性组合；对于不可合并的指标，则通过提供受辛普森悖论启发的反例作为正式的反证。结果：五个性能指标（AUC、校准截距、校准斜率等）……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究系统考察了临床预测AI中15个常用性能指标的可合并性，发现包括AUC在内的五个指标是不可合并的（即总体性能不等于亚组性能的加权平均），这对基于亚组的公平性评估具有重要警示意义。
en_tdlr: This study systematically examines the collapsibility of 15 commonly reported performance metrics in clinical predictive AI, showing that five metrics including AUC are non-collapsible—overall performance does not equal the weighted average of subgroup values—with important implications for subgroup-based fairness evaluation.
